name.description: group.action; CLI `reqseq group action`, API `POST /v1/commands/group.action`, MCP tool `group_action`.

title.description: The name of the command for people, English, sentence case, unique in the catalog: what the app's command prompt offers (SR-108, SR-073 AK2) and the MCP tool `title`. When an app action does the same, the title is the action's name, so the prompt lists it once. Free of delete words except for relations (D-045).

summary.description: What the command does and what for, in one or two sentences in the user's words: the command reference, its index, `--help`, the MCP tool description and the OpenAPI summary show it. At most 50 words, counted as the text split at white space (`catalog-checks.mjs`, #1252).

details.description: What a user needs to know beyond the summary: rules, cases and limits of the command. Shown on the command's reference page below the summary, not in the index, `--help` or the MCP tool list (#1252). Implementation notes belong in the block files of `packages/core/docs/`.

effect.description: No command writes to Git (D-036). No command deletes elements (D-045).

whileReadOnly.description: Whether a `write-files` command runs while the workspace is read-only (a missing or faulty metamodel, SR-011 AK3): `refuse` gives `workspace.read-only` before the command runs, `allow` runs it (`workspace.init`, which creates the workspace). Required for `write-files`, not allowed for `read` (reads always run). Each command's SR decides; until then `refuse` (ADR-0002 rule 5, ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#142).

whileReadOnlyReason.description: Why the command has its `whileReadOnly` value, in one line for the people who change it. Required with `whileReadOnly`.

stage.description: The stage of the delivery plan in which the command is built.

arguments.description: How a command prompt asks for the input (SR-108 AK4): every top-level property of `input` exactly once, the required ones first, in the order they are asked. `complete` says where the values to offer come from (a closed list; the app maps each source to read commands of core and decides nothing about what is allowed; `folder` and `file` map to `workspace.listFolder`, the one read command made for completion, because only core reads the file system). `of` names an earlier field the source depends on. Without it, the nearest earlier field of the fitting source, never an `element` field with a `meaning`: an `element` or `relationTarget` field for status, invalidStatus, relationKind, hint and property (relation also a `relation` field); an `element` field for criterion and elementFile; a `relationKind` field for relationTarget; a `property` field for value; a `type` field for properties and relations; a `folder` field for metamodelLocation. With no such field, status, invalidStatus, relationKind, hint and property give every value of the metamodel or the workspace; the others need one. `validate-schemas.mjs` checks the coverage, the order, `of` and the fields each source fits (`catalog-checks.mjs`).

complete.description: element: elements found by element.search; with `meaning`, the elements of the types with that meaning (metamodel.get, then element.list), as view offers the variants, without `core`. type: types of the metamodel. status: statuses of the type of the element in `of` (without it, every status of the metamodel). invalidStatus: of those, the ones the metamodel marks invalid. relationKind: kinds that relation.options allows from the element in `of` (without it, every relation kind of the metamodel). relationTarget: elements of the target types of the kind in `of` (element.search with selection.where.type). relation: with `of` an element field, the kinds of the existing relations of that element; with `of` a relation field (the kind asked before), the targets of the relations of that kind (relation.remove: source, kind, target). property: properties of the type of the element in `of` (every property of the metamodel without it). value: the values the metamodel fixes for the property in `of`. hint: open hints of the element in `of` (without it, every open hint). filter: saved filters. baseline: baselines (baseline.list). perspective: perspectives (perspective.list). view: `core` and the variants of the workspace (element.list of the types with the meaning `variant`). repository: repositories of the workspace. selection: the selection of the list shown. choice: the `enum` of the property or of its items, inline or in the definition its `$ref` names (`hint.list` `kind`: the problem codes of `common.schema.json`). folder: a `localPath` field that names a folder, file: one that names a file; both completed with the entries of the typed folder (workspace.listFolder, files only for file), and every `localPath` field has one of them (`catalog-checks.mjs`). criterion: the acceptance criteria of the element in `of` (element.get `criterionReferences`), each by its key where it has one, else by its number (SR-029 AK13). evidenceLocation: the evidence locations of the workspace (workspace.status `evidence[].folder`); typed text stays, for a folder below one. elementFile: the file of the element in `of` (element.get), or, when the reference is ambiguous, the files of the elements it names (`details.candidates` of `ref.ambiguous`, the answer of the same read command). metamodelLocation: an object `{ repository?, path }`, asked in two steps: the repository (the main repository the default), then the path (in the main repository the folders below the folder in `of`, workspace.listFolder; typed text accepted). group: a `groupKey` field: `type`, `status`, `package` (when the meaning `packages` is assigned) and the properties element.facets gives values for. Composed values, each one flat entry whose field's schema fixes the parts (`catalog-checks.mjs` binds them): condition: a `condition` field of `filter.schema.json`, built from parts: types, statuses and properties with their values (metamodel.get, element.facets over the conditions chosen before), verification and validation status (their enums), validity (core and the variants, as view), relations (the relation kinds of metamodel.get and the `relationCondition` enums) and text. sort: a list of `sortKey`: the keys of its `by` enum and the metamodel.get properties that hold no relations, each with an order from its enum. properties: an object of `inputValue` by property key: the properties of the type in `of` (metamodel.get) without the title and those given, each value as value gives it. relations: a `relationRefs` field: the kinds metamodel.get `relationKinds` gives for the type in `of`, then elements of their target types (element.search). text, number, boolean: typed free input. json: any other object or mixed field, typed as JSON and checked by core.

meaning.description: Only on an `element` source: the field takes an element whose type has this meaning (`variant`, D-020; `package`, D-040), and its values are those elements. A field with a meaning is never the nearest earlier field a source without `of` reads, so `evidence.record criteria` reads `ref`, not `variant`; an explicit `of` may name it (`catalog-checks.mjs`).

replaces.description: Earlier optional fields a value of this field takes the place of: the prompt leaves them out of the input when this field has a value other than `false`, so they only said what it offers. `hint.confirm`: hints chosen at `hintIds` confirm only those, not every hint `ref`, `target` and `kind` select (#291); `all` yes confirms those of the workspace, not those of the shown element as `ref` (#644). `catalog-checks.mjs` checks the fields.

flag.description: Name of the CLI flag, without `--`, when it is not the field name in kebab-case (ADR-0009): `element.create` takes its `properties` as `--set key=value`, as `element.update` takes `set`. Not the name of another field's flag, nor of a common option (`validate-schemas.mjs`, `catalog-checks.mjs`).

items.description: A top-level array of `output`: one line per item.

fields.description: Top-level fields of `output` that every line carries before the keys of its item, in this order; a field the output leaves out is left out of the lines too. None is an array or a property of the item schema (`catalog-checks.mjs`).

jsonLines.description: The command also gives its output as JSON Lines (one compact JSON object and LF per line, UTF-8): the CLI with `--jsonl`, the API with `Accept: application/x-ndjson` (ADR-0009). Each line is the listed `fields` of the output, then one item of `items`; the other top-level fields are not in the lines. MCP and the app keep the JSON object (ADR-0002 rule 3, #319).

textOutput.description: A required top-level `string` field of `output` (`catalog-checks.mjs`) that is the command's text: the CLI prints exactly this string to stdout without `--json` or `--yaml`, and the problems alone to stderr (ADR-0009). API, MCP and the app keep the JSON object (ADR-0002 rule 3, SR-151 AK4).

output.description: Outputs are JSON objects and say so at the root, also next to a `$ref`: MCP needs `type: object` at the root of an output schema (ADR-0009).
